Issue: test_local_user and local_readonly_user are both created using ${test_user_password} (TestPwd123). Using the same password makes it harder to confirm that a test is failing because of a role restriction rather than a credential issue. A dedicated variable for the readonly user password (e.g. ${local_readonly_password}) would make each user's credentials independently traceable in logs.

Fix: Add a separate variable ${local_readonly_user_password} TestPwd123 (can share the same value initially but makes each credential independently overridable) and use it in Redfish Create User ${local_readonly_user} ${local_readonly_user_password} ... and Redfish.Login ${local_readonly_user} ${local_readonly_user_password}.

Why: Improves test clarity and makes credential-related failures easier to diagnose independently.
Done

Fix: Move the explanatory note into the [Documentation] block so it is unmistakably associated with the teardown override:
```
[Documentation]  Verify LDAP admin user creates local users with different privileges,
...  then test privilege modification by local admin user (should succeed) and
...  local readonly user (should be forbidden due to insufficient permissions).
...  Note: Teardown uses FFDC only — Redfish session is restored inside the FINALLY
...  block of the template keyword to guarantee cleanup on every iteration.

```
Why: Keeps the intent visible in the canonical documentation field rather than a comment that blends with template data rows, and prevents future maintainers from accidentally re-adding Redfish.Login to the teardown and creating a double-login.
